questions.question: A pacemaker must deliver a pacing pulse within 10 ms or the patient is harmed. What class of real-time requirement is this?
questions.explanation: Missing the deadline causes catastrophic harm, making this a hard real-time requirement where any missed deadline equals total failure.

questions.question: A master must poll five different sensors but only two shared wires are available. Which protocol fits?
questions.explanation: I2C supports multiple addressed slave devices on the same two wires (SDA and SCL), unlike SPI which needs a select line per slave.

questions.question: An MCU must stream pixel data to a display at maximum speed with simultaneous readback. Which protocol fits best?
questions.explanation: SPI's full-duplex MOSI/MISO transfer and high clock rates make it the best choice for bandwidth-heavy peripherals like displays.

questions.question: A UART link is configured at 9600 baud. How many bits per second does it transmit?
questions.explanation: In standard UART signaling each symbol carries one bit, so 9600 baud equals 9600 bits per second including start and stop bits.

questions.question: Firmware deadlocks in an infinite loop after a rare sensor fault. What hardware feature recovers the system automatically?
questions.explanation: Because the hung firmware can no longer refresh the watchdog, the timer expires and triggers a hardware reset to restore operation.

questions.question: A battery-powered sensor node sleeps 99% of the time and wakes once per hour to transmit. What is this power-saving pattern called?
questions.explanation: Duty cycling keeps the node in deep sleep for most of its lifetime and activates it briefly, stretching battery life from days to years.

questions.question: A 10-bit ADC uses a 3.3 V reference. What is the approximate voltage resolution per step?
questions.explanation: Resolution = Vref / 2^10 = 3.3 V / 1024 steps ≈ 0.00322 V, or about 3.22 mV per least significant bit.

questions.question: A PWM output at 25% duty cycle on a 5 V pin produces what average voltage?
questions.explanation: Average voltage = duty cycle × supply = 0.25 × 5 V = 1.25 V, which is how PWM dims LEDs or controls motor speed.

questions.question: What is the term for the delay between an interrupt request and the start of its handler?
questions.explanation: Interrupt latency is the time from the interrupt signal to the first instruction of the ISR; RTOSs work to minimize and bound it.

questions.question: A project needs JPEG decoding, networking, and a camera interface. Which board fits better — Arduino or Raspberry Pi?
questions.explanation: Image decoding and networking demand a microprocessor-class device running a full OS; a microcontroller board like Arduino lacks the memory and compute.

questions.question: A UART frame has 1 start bit, 8 data bits, and 1 stop bit. At 9600 baud, what is the maximum payload throughput in bytes per second?
questions.explanation: Each byte requires 10 frame bits (1 start + 8 data + 1 stop), so 9600 / 10 = 960 bytes per second of usable payload.

questions.question: A glucose monitor must sample its sensor every second without ever missing a deadline. Which OS category is required?
questions.explanation: Only an RTOS provides the deterministic scheduling guarantees needed to never miss the sampling deadline; a general-purpose OS cannot.

questions.question: I2C bus lines float when no device drives them low. What components are required on SDA and SCL for correct operation?
questions.explanation: I2C uses open-drain outputs that can only pull lines low; external pull-up resistors return the bus to the high state when released.

questions.question: A motor controller must respond to encoder edges within microseconds; a full OS adds too much jitter. What class of processor fits?
questions.explanation: A bare-metal or RTOS-based microcontroller offers deterministic microsecond interrupt response that a general-purpose OS on a microprocessor cannot.

questions.question: Power fails halfway through flashing a device's firmware. What feature lets the device recover from the corrupted image?
questions.explanation: A protected bootloader (often with a fallback or dual image bank) runs first at startup and can re-flash a valid image after a failed update.
